newsitem.title: USA: Foreign buying of U.S. securities weakens in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying of U.S. securities weakens in Q1.

text.p: Foreign purchases of U.S. securities weakened to an average $22.806 billion a month during the first quarter of this year from $30.089 billion in the final three months of last year, a Treasury Department report on Monday indicated.
The information was contained in the quarterly Treasury Bulletin, which calculates foreigners' purchases of long-term securities as reported by banks and brokers in the United States.
During March, foreign purchases of U.S. securities fell to $20.637 billion from $25.556 billion in February and from $22.225 billion in January.
The report covers foreign buying of not only marketable U.S. Treasury bonds and notes but also bonds issued by U.S. companies and securities of American corporations.

Among the biggest purchasers of marketable U.S. Treasury bonds and notes during the first quarter was Britain, which bought a net $23.25 billion worth over the three months, up from $18.19 billion in last year's fourth quarter.
But Japan trimmed its purchases of Treasury bonds and notes to $12.86 billion during the first quarter from $15.44 billion in the fourth quarter last year.
Canada increased its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities by a slim $342 million in the first quarter after reducing them by $2.55 billion in last year's fourth quarter.
Germany sold down its holdings in the first quarter this year by $3.99 billion after raising them by $7.34 billion in the fourth quarter last year.
The United States depends upon strong foreign buying of U.S. government securities, which are obligations to pay in future, to help finance the total government debt that now exceeds $5 trillion.
